triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a pure identifier rename and failed: the one input `entry_is_line_a` is split across rules into `entry_is_china_301_list123` (line 2994) and `entry_is_section_122_exempt` (line 2572), and `entry_is_line_b` into `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, `entry_is_china_301_2024_action` and `entry_is_section_232_covered`, so the §122 exclusion condition genuinely changes which entries are zeroed rather than just being renamed. The rule's own unchanged proof atoms ground version[1] on the "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and on "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles"; resolving us/statute/hts/9903.03.03 through the pinned release confirms the §122 carve-out is that article list ("Articles the product of any country, as provided for in subdivision (aa)(ii) of U.S. note 2 to this subchapter"), with no basis for excusing an article because it sits on a China §301 list. So the pre-fix branch was a condition with no source basis in the chapter-wide composition and the fix re-grounds it on the source's own carve-outs — untraceable_branch, and the PR body independently states the coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins."
